The net bill was USD 10.0 billion in October 2025. Crude imports alone cost USD 19.5 billion, against USD 10.4 billion a year ago, even though volumes rose only 11 per cent to 23.3 million tonnes. LNG imports cost USD 1.3 billion, and petroleum product exports brought in USD 6.3 billion. Brent averaged USD 116.77 in September and USD 64.75 in October 2025. The Indian basket averaged USD 119.91 in October, against USD 65.08 a year earlier. Over April-October, the net import bill reached USD 97.7 billion, up from USD 70.3 billion a year earlier. Crude imports rose 2.7 per cent in volume but cost USD 111.0 billion, against USD 72.3 billion. Consumption of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) fell 12.3 per cent in October

title: India, Canada conclude sixth round of talks for proposed trade pact
description: India and Canada have concluded the sixth round of negotiations for a trade agreement, aimed at unlocking new opportunities in trade and investment, and diversifying supply chains, an official statement said on Saturday. The negotiations covered key areas, including trade in goods, trade in services, rules of origin, trade remedies, intellectual property and investment promotion, the commerce ministry said. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal held a meeting with Glenn Purves, Vice Minister of International Trade of Canada, and his delegation to review the progress of negotiations for the proposed Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA). The ten-day talks concluded on November 20. "Both sides reaffirmed their shared commitment to concluding an ambitious, balanced and commercially meaningful agreement that delivers tangible benefits to farmers, industries, businesses and Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in both countries," it said.
